candidate.answerReason: For integers n≥0 and 0≤k≤n, choosing k objects uniquely specifies the complementary n−k objects. Thus C(n,k)=C(n,n−k), the identity in option B.

methods.label: Use complementary selections
methods.explanation: Selecting \(k\) objects and leaving \(k\) objects are two sides of the same thing, so \(C(n,k)=C(n,n-k)\).
methods.levelReason: The argument uses only unordered selection and the symmetry property of combination numbers.
